original_question: Let Omega be a bounded open convex subset of R^d with Lipschitz boundary and 0 in its interior. For 0 <= beta < d and f : Z^d -> R, define the discrete centered fractional maximal operator associated to Omega by M_{Omega,beta} f(n) = sup_{r>=0} N(0,r)^{beta/d - 1} sum_{m in Omega(0,r)} |f(n+m)|, where N(x,r) counts lattice points in the Omega-ball Omega(x,r). When 0 <= beta < 1 and q = d/(d-beta), does every discrete function f satisfy ||∇M_{Omega,beta} f||_{ell^q(Z^d)} <= C(d,Omega,beta) ||∇f||_{ell^1(Z^d)}? More generally, does inequality (6.4) hold for all alpha <= beta and q = d/(d-beta+alpha)? The paper asks the analogous questions for the uncentered operator as well.
target_in_paper: Question 11 in §6.2 ("Multidimensional results"), immediately after the definitions of the multidimensional discrete fractional maximal operators associated to a convex set Ω, Theorem 6.4, and the necessary scaling condition (6.5).
correct_elements: Your draft is very close to the paper-faithful target. It correctly identifies the multidimensional discrete fractional maximal operator associated to a bounded open convex set Ω with Lipschitz boundary and 0 in int(Ω); it places the question in the hard range 0 ≤ β < 1; it gives the critical exponent q = d/(d-β) for the endpoint gradient estimate; it recognizes the more general α-parameter version with q = d/(d-β+α); and it notes that the paper asks the analogous question for the uncentered operator as well.
missing_details: The nearest official formulation in the paper is not a theorem or conjecture in the introduction but Question 11 in §6.2; the draft should identify that exact target.
The draft references inequality (6.4) without stating it explicitly. To be stand-alone, it should spell out the general inequality rather than cite its label only.
The discrete gradient ∇ is not defined. In this setting one should specify ∇f(n) = (f(n+e1)-f(n), ..., f(n+ed)-f(n)).
The lattice Ω-balls and counting function should be defined explicitly, not only informally through Ω(0,r) and N(0,r).
The role of the uncentered operator should be stated precisely if it is included, rather than only mentioned loosely.

The quantifier on f should be made stand-alone: at minimum, one should indicate that the question concerns discrete functions f : Z^d → R for which the right-hand side of the proposed estimate is finite; in the α-generalization this also implicitly brings in the ℓ^1-norm of f.

The nearby paper context matters: Theorem 6.4 gives only non-endpoint approximations to the desired bound, and (6.5) gives the necessary critical relation q = d/(d-β+α); that is why Question 11 is phrased exactly at that exponent.
refined_question: Let Ω ⊂ R^d be a bounded open convex set with Lipschitz boundary and 0 ∈ int(Ω). For x ∈ Z^d and r ≥ 0, let Ω(x,r) denote the discrete Ω-ball of center x and radius r, and let N(x,r) = #Ω(x,r). For 0 ≤ β < d and f : Z^d → R, define the centered discrete fractional maximal operator associated to Ω by M_{Ω,β}f(n) = sup_{r≥0} N(0,r)^{β/d-1} ∑_{m∈Ω(0,r)} |f(n+m)|, and define the discrete gradient by ∇f(n) = (f(n+e_1)-f(n), ..., f(n+e_d)-f(n)). In the open range 0 ≤ β < 1, is it true that with q = d/(d-β) one has the endpoint estimate ||∇M_{Ω,β}f||_{ℓ^q(Z^d)} ≤ C(d,Ω,β) ||∇f||_{ℓ^1(Z^d)} for every discrete function f for which the right-hand side is finite? More generally, for 0 ≤ α ≤ β < 1 and q = d/(d-β+α), does the critical inequality ||∇M_{Ω,β}f||_{ℓ^q(Z^d)} ≤ C(d,Ω,α,β) ||∇f||_{ℓ^1(Z^d)}^{1-α} ||f||_{ℓ^1(Z^d)}^α hold? The same question is asked in the paper for the uncentered discrete fractional maximal operator \widetilde{M}_{Ω,β}.
justification: The draft is clearly targeting the paper's Question 11 in §6.2, not a broader neighboring problem. The official question is asked only after the paper defines the multidimensional discrete centered/uncentered fractional maximal operators attached to a convex set Ω, recalls Theorem 6.4 as the current partial result, and then derives the necessary critical exponent relation (6.5). Your first sentence matches the operator and the endpoint range 0 ≤ β < 1; your second sentence matches the paper's exact generalization from the endpoint case to the α-parameter family tied to the critical scaling q = d/(d-β+α). The main incompleteness is that your draft refers to (6.4) without stating it, and it leaves implicit the discrete gradient and the precise discrete Ω-ball notation.
